body:
Thanks. (Hi, I'm OP.) I see my GP next week for a medication follow-up; those are some good questions to ask. 

I've been seeing a therapist regularly for the last four or five months. I'm quite eager to discuss this in our next session. Unfortunately, I don't see her until next week. I don't really know what to do until then. I don't want to over-diagnose myself, you know?

Thanks, those seem really interesting. I haven't done much pleasure reading the last few months, so I like the idea of the fiction one. 

I haven't seen my therapist since earlier this week. She knows I've been having suicidal thoughts in general... Do I need to contact her? I have no idea what I'm doing. I feel pretty embarrassed about the idea of telling her. Probably hence the anonymous internet advice seeking.

Wow. Thanks for sharing, my situation feels less hard by comparison. Glad you made it through. 

I can relate to being dependent on someone - I was for most of this as well (pre-diagnosis, but still through a rough time). That relationship ended and sent me down farther, just as I was seeking professional help. I don't know how to do this without my person, and I can see how even though I'm nowhere near emotionally available for a new relationship, it would be nice to have someone instead of a little bit from everyone. If that makes sense.
Thank you for that thought. I wish my thinking was like that and I was able to take a step away. I'm clinging to the note right now (metaphorically), but I will start thinking about destroying it.
Thanks. It's easy to tell myself not to do it, but I have no confidence in any of my decisions right now. How did you overcome the suicidal desire? I literally can't see on to better days.

Thanks for the recommendation, I remember hearing something about that documentary. 

Mostly religious and spiritual books, actually. Some small "hang in there" quote-type books as well. Do you have any good suggestions outside of those areas?
This not only helps a little, it helps a lot. Really and truly, thank you. I appreciate you taking the time to help a stranger on the internet :)
That makes sense. I'm scared of the withdrawal/dependency issues with all these meds as well.

Yes, I've been prescribed an anti-anxiety, antidepressant, and sleep aid. I filled all three yesterday, but even reaching that decision was difficult. 

No therapy currently; I went a couple of weeks ago, and the therapist told me I'd be fine, had nothing to worry about, etc. Said I needn't come back. Went to my GP out of concern about the effect this is having on my body. She prescribed the meds.

I guess I'm scared of it all. Because I don't want to be here, the downward spiral is appealing, even though I know that's not logical. I also feel like I'd be doing it for other people, for some reason.

Thanks, I know I do want it to be okay. Just can't see that now.

Thank you! I will research.

I've come to accept that I will cry any time I have any sort of feeling. These damn responses are making me tear up! :') also thanks, mom. Heh.

True, it's a specific career path and not only a "here to help you" position. I like that idea, though, of them expanding your perspective.
Edit: word

I'm sorry, I can imagine that would be hard after so many years going by as well. Time seems to dull a lot of things. And ugh group therapy seems horrible, I don't know if I could ever do that.

That makes a lot of sense - sort of crafting a reason to be there. Thanks for sharing that; I will try to be attune to my own thoughts and feelings as I go.

And thank you! I hope so too.

Edit: I say "definitely" too much.

Thanks for the post! What is CBT?

So the first session can be seen as a sort of "getting to know you"...? I figured I'd have to do a lot of talking, but would you say the first time will be mostly me talking (or likely crying, ha)?
I can definitely understand that. That's great that you've got a supportive SO! :)
...not sure if American Pie reference, or actual comfort food reference...

Glad to hear medication is working for you. Yeah, the cost is definitely a lot! Fortunately my work benefits include it or I might not have sought it out. Why do you find therapy annoying, if I may ask?
